title: Opening the first object
why: Obtain module and result names through the portable argument services, then open the selected first object read-only and close its owned handle.

title: Refilling a bounded input block
why: Read through a 1024-byte block and consume every positive read before refilling. Zero count is EOF; Control-Z ends object text.

title: Reading one physical record
why: Bound a physical record to 120 characters, count its line, and accept ordinary DOS text endings without retaining the complete object.

title: Recognizing the object envelope
why: Recognize OBJ1 and END, including blank lines and semicolon comments. Reject unknown records instead of silently copying malformed text.

title: Writing literal bytes
why: Decode up to sixteen hexadecimal bytes in a B record and stream them to an owned LINK.TMP. Inspect that file before deleting it.

title: Publishing the accepted image

title: Placing two modules
why: Place MAIN.OBJ first and UTIL.OBJ second. Count both modules on pass one, then reopen them and stream the same layout on pass two.

title: Recording public names
why: Record complete public spellings and module-relative offsets in initialized forty-byte records. Check duplicates, extents and pass agreement.
